title: Short but genuine answers cannot be quoted: the strict verifier's 12-code-point / 2-token minimum turns 'Yes.', 'In March.' or 'Friday.' into an unanswered Q&A
evidence: In the drop path an answer whose only evidence is a quote under 12 code points or 2 tokens is refused (`too-short`), so the entry is emitted as `unanswered` with null answer. The schema's own fixture (schema/fixtures/session_pages/valid-grounded.json) uses the answer 'In March.' (9 chars), which this path could never emit as answered. Safe direction (no fake evidence) but loses real answers. Policy owner decision: allow a short quote only when it equals a whole turn, or accept the loss. Not changed here (the verifier is merged, checked code).

title: Verified quotes can still drop a negation or qualifier: the sentence-span rule the verifier manifest says a wiring unit must add is NOT enforced
evidence: qa/manifests/t040-strict-quote-verifier-and-windowing.md (Fix cycle 1, 'READ THIS FIRST' point 2) says a wiring unit must require the quote to span a whole sentence/clause or display the surrounding sentence. This unit does not: 'I do not think it is safe' can be emitted as an insight whose verified quote is 'think it is safe'. Mitigation present: every item is labelled verification 'unverified' and the independent judge sees the full adjacent context and rejects unsupported/miscategorised items, but the judge is a model. Needs a policy decision (sentence-aligned quotes only, vs. showing the surrounding turn at render time via the cited turnId). CHECKER REPRODUCTION (end to end, fake model, dropUnverified+strictWebinar, judge passing everything): source turn t1 "We do not recommend applying in March"; model item {kind:insight,text:"recommend applying in March",evidence:[{t1,"recommend applying in March"}]} SHIPS: citedItems[0].text and evidence quote both "recommend applying in March", dropped=[], degraded=null. The text==quotes rule (extractiveText) only compares the item text with its own quotes, so an extractive item whose quote omits the negation passes it; the opposite-meaning statement is emitted with a verbatim, verifier-passed citation. Same for "I do not think it is safe to wait" -> "think it is safe to wait" (2 of 2 shipped). A paraphrase text ("Apply in March") is dropped, so the exposure is exactly the verbatim-fragment case. Raised to high by the checker: a wrong-meaning citation is shipped as evidence; the only guard is a model judge.

title: A quote that straddles a 4000-character span cut, or sits in a cut word, is dropped (false drop)
evidence: runtimeWindows slices an oversized turn into 4000-char spans at arbitrary offsets. The drop path requires the quote to lie entirely inside one submitted span and to start/end at word boundaries, so a sentence crossing a cut can never be emitted from that turn. Fail-closed, only for turns over 4000 chars. Not changed (windowing is merged, checked code).

title: The roadmap's 'numbers' have no category: CitedItem.kind is insight|decision|action and no field carries numbers
evidence: T-040 asks for summary, facts, numbers, Q&A, action items. The merged schema has no number kind; numeric statements ride as insights (citedItems) or claims, and session_pages.numericFacts is an untouched free-form legacy array. Not invented here; a schema decision for the Approver.

title: dropUnverified is not switched on by any caller; the live webinar runner is untouched (D-119) and process-video buildNotes still returns empty decisions/actions
evidence: indexSession accepts `dropUnverified` (with strictWebinar) but apps/api/src/composition/production.ts buildIndexer and scripts/webinar/sync-session.mjs do not pass it, so no production path uses the drop mode yet. ISS-WEBINARRELEASE-001's first recorded reproduction (scripts/webinar/process-video.mjs buildNotes returns decisions:[] and actionItems:[]) is therefore NOT addressed by this unit.

title: Sentence-span floor is bypassed by abbreviation periods: a negation before U.S., e.g., vs., approx. or Dr. lands in a different sentence, so a negation-dropping quote ships as verified
evidence: CHECKER REPRODUCTIONS on sentenceSpanProblem at 1f5bf4b (all return null = would ship through resolveEvidence): 'I do not think e.g. March works for everyone.' quote 'March works for everyone.'; 'We do not accept applications from the U.S. after March first.' quote 'after March first.'; 'We do not recommend it vs. applying in March works.' quote 'applying in March works.'; 'We do not recommend this approx. 3.5 lakh fee.' quote '3.5 lakh fee.'; 'He said we do not recommend it, Dr. Rao recommends applying in March.' quote 'Rao recommends applying in March.'. Cause: sentenceStart/sentenceEnd treat every period followed by whitespace as a sentence break, so the negation sits in a 'previous sentence' and the floor never sees it; the start rule is satisfied because the quote starts after a period. Fix direction: do not break after known abbreviations or single-letter-dot sequences (U.S., e.g., i.e., Dr., Mr., vs., approx., etc.), or scan the markers over the whole turn text before the quote up to the last ? ! or a period followed by a capital non-abbreviation word; pin with these 5 strings.

title: sentence-span.ts: MARKER regex loses its p-escapes in a plain string; question-only quotes ship; curly n't branch unpinned
evidence: (a) MARKER is built with new RegExp over a normal string containing backslash-p{L}, which the string literal turns into plain p{L}; the lookaround class becomes [p{L}p{N}_]: 'xnot' and 'l/not' match (false positives, safe) but a marker glued to p, l, n, { or } (e.g. 'notp') is missed; use String.raw. (b) 'Apply in March? Absolutely not.' quote 'Apply in March?' and 'Should we apply in March? Definitely not!' quote 'Should we apply in March?' pass (negative answer in the next sentence). (c) Mutation replacing the curly n-apostrophe-t branch with the straight one SURVIVES the 18 notes tests: don-curly-t / won-curly-t is handled correctly but no test pins it.

title: Unlisted abbreviation followed by a capitalised word is still a sentence break, so a negation before Pvt./Univ./Asst./Ave. ships a meaning-reversed quote (ISS-T040GEN-006 closed only for the listed abbreviations)
evidence: CHECKER REPRODUCTIONS on sentenceSpanProblem at ff696ba (null = ships; enumerating every word-aligned quote): 'We do not accept Pvt. Colleges applications after March first.' ships 'Colleges applications after March first.'; 'I do not recommend Univ. Admissions in March for everyone.' ships 'Admissions in March for everyone.'; 'We never take Asst. Professors in March for this program.' ships 'Professors in March for this program.'; 'I do not think Ave. Road students apply in March.' ships 'Road students apply in March.'; 'I do not think the Pkwy. Campus works for everyone in March.' ships 'Campus works for everyone in March.'; 'We do not apply in the Q1. March works for everyone else.' ships 'March works for everyone else.'. Cause: isBoundary() breaks on any period whose word is not in the 70-word list, not single-letter, and is followed by a capital; the claim 'any doubt = no break' holds only for listed words. Pvt./Univ. are ordinary in Indian-education English (this corpus: 'Mr.' x23, 'Dr.' x9). Verified fine: Govt., Corp., Inc., a.k.a., approx (no dot), Mr. Not Sure, B.Tech., p.m., Jan./Mar./Sat., ellipsis, newline, parentheses, quotes, '3.5 not 4', Hinglish nahi + Dr./approx., danda, fullwidth period. Fix direction: when the period follows a short capitalised or all-letter word not in a known sentence-final set, also scan the preceding clause for markers (fail closed), or require a break only after a lower-case/complete word followed by a capital AND no marker in the preceding 12 words; pin with these 6 strings.

title: negated-by-reply and the marker list are lexical: a one-word non-marker rejection ('Wrong.', 'Incorrect.', 'I disagree.', 'Bad idea.', 'That is false.') after a quote still ships the quote
evidence: CHECKER REPRODUCTIONS at ff696ba: 'Apply in March. Wrong.' ships 'Apply in March.'; 'Apply in March. Incorrect.' ships 'Apply in March.'; 'Apply in March. I disagree.', 'Apply in March. That is false.', 'Apply in March. Bad idea.' each ship 'Apply in March.'; 'He is wrong; apply in March.' ships 'apply in March.'. Reply marker list covers not/no/never/nope/nah/none/nothing/nowhere/neither/nor/cannot/nahi/nahin/n't only. Lower severity than 008: the reply needs a second speaker-like turn inside the same turn text and the negation is not in the quote's own sentence. Fix direction: add wrong/false/incorrect/disagree/untrue/nonsense/bad idea to NEG_REPLY (short replies only).

title: Unlisted LOWER-CASE abbreviation followed by a capitalised word is still a sentence break (cycle-3 boundary rule is structural only for capitalised/dotted/mixed tokens)
evidence: CHECKER at 0ae7fe7 (null = ships): "We do not accept pvt. Colleges applications after March first." ships "Colleges applications after March first."; same for univ. Colleges, mgmt. Quota, pg. Courses (all lower-case, none in LOWER_ABBREVIATIONS). Corpus data/toc-migrated (3427 turns): 0 occurrences of an unlisted lower-case abbreviation + capital (only etc 40 and genuine no. 14), so exotic, not measured loss. fix_direction: do not break after a lower-case word when the sentence so far contains a marker unless the next sentence also starts after a real end, or keep merging when token length <=4 and followed by a capitalised non-pronoun.

title: A statement followed by a rejection that is not a lexical negation (Wrong./Incorrect./I disagree./Ignore that.) or longer than 5 words still ships the statement when the statement ends in a lower-case word
evidence: CHECKER at 0ae7fe7: "Fees are 1000 rupees. Wrong." ships "Fees are 1000 rupees."; "Fees are 1000 rupees. Ignore that." ships it; "Fees are 1000 rupees. Not for freshers at this college though." ships it (reply > MAX_REPLY_WORDS). Statements ending in a capitalised word ("Apply in March. Wrong.") are now merged and no longer ship alone. Known gap named by the maker; rated medium: needs a lower-case-ending short statement plus a non-lexical rejection in the same turn; item still carries verification unverified and goes through the independent judge. fix_direction: judge-side check of the following sentence, not a larger word list.

title: Unlisted lower-case abbreviation with the negation AFTER it: the left fragment still ships and drops the negation (ISS-T040GEN-010 rule looks only left of the dot)
evidence: CHECKER at 6f0e88a (null = ships): "Admission is open for pvt. Colleges do not take March applications." ships "Admission is open for pvt."; also "Seats are open in pvt. Colleges but not in govt ones." -> "Seats are open in pvt." and "... pvt. Colleges only if you apply early.". Manifest claim that a wrong break with no marker on the left cannot hide a negation is false for the left-hand quote. Pre-existing at HEAD but inside the stated fix for -010. fix_direction: also merge (no break) when MARKER occurs between the dot and the next real boundary; re-measure recall cost (-010 currently costs 11.4 points sentence).
